proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity at Section 12(b) covers only its own breach of this Agreement, so it leaves us exposed on third-party IP infringement claims against the Interface and hosted services we are required to use. We have added the vendor-side IP, breach-of-law, data-breach and wilful misconduct indemnity with the usual notice/control/cooperation procedure and carve-outs for Client Content and Client modifications; an IP-only indemnity with the customary exclusions and remedies would be our fallback.

ops.text: c. Without limiting Section 12(b), TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates, directors, officers, employees and agents from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any deliverable provided by TrueLink infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (ii) TrueLink's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink; or (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The indemnified party shall promptly notify the indemnifying party of any such claim, the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement thereof (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation on the indemnified party shall be made without its prior written consent), and the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. TrueLink's obligations under clause (i) shall not apply to the extent the claim arises from Client Content or from Client's modification of the Interface contrary to TrueLink's written instructions.

proposal.summary: Add TrueLink IP infringement / misconduct indemnity with standard defence procedure

quote: b. TrueLink shall indemnify and hold Client harmless, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to any
rationale: Section 12(b) limits TrueLink's indemnity to claims arising out of its own breach of the Agreement or failure to perform its obligations; there is no indemnity for third-party allegations that the Interface or hosted services infringe intellectual property rights (and no non-infringement warranty anywhere else in the Agreement — the only infringement covenants run in TrueLink's favour or against Client at §§ 2 and 8(e)). That fails even the fallback, which requires a vendor IP indemnity, while Client's indemnity in § 12(a) is broad (Client breach, Web Site/Client Content, and injury or damage from anything transmitted from the Web Site). We therefore inserted a new § 12(c) giving the preferred vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content/Credit Data and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and Client Content and Client-modification carve-outs. We have left § 12(a) as drafted rather than narrowing it, keeping the edit minimal.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an ownership provision confirming that Client retains all rights in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property and data submitted through the Interface, and that customizations and other results of the Support Services are owned by Client with a licence back of any embedded TrueLink IP. Our playbook requires us to own what we pay for and everything we put in, with no assignment or joint ownership of our IP or data; TrueLink's ownership of the Interface is expressly preserved. If ownership of customizations is an issue, we can accept TrueLink ownership of generic tools plus a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the results for our business.

ops.text: e. Client Ownership. As between the parties, Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client Intellectual Property, and all data submitted to or transmitted through the Interface or the Web Site by or on behalf of Client or its customers or brokers (including Credit Data, subject only to the nonexclusive license granted in Section 8(d)). All results of the Support Services and any customizations, modifications, programs or other materials created by TrueLink specifically for Client hereunder shall be the sole property of Client, and TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein. TrueLink retains all ownership rights in the TrueLink Intellectual Property and the Interface, and to the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in such results, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the same in connection with Client's business. Nothing herein creates any joint ownership of, or any right of TrueLink in, Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or Client's data.

proposal.summary: Add Client ownership of Client Content, data and Support Services work product, with licence back of embedded TrueLink IP and no joint ownership.

quote: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
rationale: The only ownership provision (§2(d)) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface and says nothing about our side of the line. There is no affirmative statement that Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or the borrower/loan data transmitted through the Interface (Client Content ownership is acknowledged only on discontinuation of hosting, in §13), and no ownership or licence provision for the results of the Support Services (i.e., the programming customization work we pay for) — §§10(b) and 10(c) treat those results only as confidential/Client Proprietary Information, which is not ownership. Combined with §8(d), under which Client grants TrueLink a worldwide licence to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit" Credit Data, the agreement leaves our data and paid-for work product without any ownership anchor, failing the fallback (which at minimum requires a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the deliverables) on a material term. We therefore inserted a minimal ownership clause: Client retains all rights in its content, IP and data (expressly preserving the existing §8(d) Credit Data licence bargain), Support Services results are assigned to Client with a perpetual licence back for any embedded TrueLink IP, TrueLink's Interface ownership is preserved, and no joint ownership is created.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the liability cap mutual and agreement-wide: as drafted only TrueLink's liability is limited (and only for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11), while Client's exposure under the broad Section 12(a) indemnity is unlimited. Our position is a mutual cap of the greater of 12 months' fees and US$1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; a straight mutual 12-month fee cap with those carve-outs is an acceptable fallback.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID OR PAYABLE BY CLIENT FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTH PERIOD AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (US$1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 12, ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; AND CLIENT'S OBLIGATION TO PAY AMOUNTS DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.

proposal.summary: Make the cap mutual and agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' fees or US$1,000,000, with standard uncapped carve-outs.

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
rationale: The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, buried in the indemnity section) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink's liability at 12 months' hosting/support compensation, while Client's liability — including under the very broad indemnity in Section 12(a) (p0071-p0072) covering any breach, Web Site/Client Content claims and third-party injury — is entirely uncapped. That is squarely in walk-away territory ("Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped") and fails the fallback, which requires a mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. There is also no defined set of carve-outs (only TrueLink's own gross negligence/wilful misconduct is excepted) and no confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap. Our redline makes the cap mutual and agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' fees and US$1,000,000 and adds a single Excluded Claims sentence. We have not added a mutual consequential-damages waiver (absent from the document), as its absence preserves our recovery against the vendor; that is noted rather than redlined.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets on notice, and made the consent standard "not unreasonably withheld", since our playbook does not permit our corporate reorganisations or M&A to be blocked. We have also confirmed that a change of control of Client is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right, and that TrueLink may not assign to a competitor of ours; if helpful we can accept a mutual successor-assignment-on-notice formulation instead.

ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, except no such approval shall be required for (a) an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or (b) an assignment by Client, upon written notice to TrueLink, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. TrueLink shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Client. No change of control of Client shall be deemed an assignment requiring approval or give rise to any right of TrueLink to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

proposal.summary: Add Client successor/M&A assignment carve-out, reasonableness standard on consent, no-competitor limit on TrueLink, and confirm change of control is not an assignment or termination trigger.

quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision (no change-of-control language appears anywhere, so TrueLink has no CoC termination or re-pricing right — that limb is satisfied). However, the clause requires the other party's prior written approval with no reasonableness standard and, critically, no carve-out for assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out exists. That fails the fallback on both material terms (successor assignment on notice, and consent not unreasonably withheld) and leaves TrueLink able to block our M&A or reorganisation. Redline adds the Client successor carve-out on notice, the reasonableness standard, a bar on TrueLink assigning to a competitor of ours, and confirms a change of control of Client is not an assignment and triggers no TrueLink right; the mutual structure of the clause is otherwise preserved.

quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation on Client. The licence grant in Section 2(a) is expressly non-exclusive and affirmatively confirms that Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system... to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink" (subject only to TrueLink's IP and Client's confidentiality obligations, which are ordinary carve-outs, not restraints on sourcing). A full-text sweep for "exclusive", "sole", "compet" and third-party procurement language turned up nothing binding Client: Section 8(d) grants TrueLink only a non-exclusive licence to Credit Data (and the referenced Non-Competition Agreement operates as a limitation on TrueLink, i.e. in our favour), and the only other "exclusive" usage is the exclusive-forum provision in Section 12. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination fee on the Client. Termination (§14) requires only that services continue, and fees be paid, through the last day of the month following notice — no fixed damages or minimum payout is triggered. Compensation (§5) contains only ordinary monthly fees for services actually requested (with blank minimum monthly amounts payable during the term, not on termination) and no late-payment penalty or fixed damages; the unsolicited e-mail covenant (§7) prohibits spamming but attaches no per-message charge or penalty to Client. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted. We note the minimum monthly fee blanks in §5a and the fact that they are excluded from Client's dispute rights in §6 as commercial points to complete, but they are not liquidated damages.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (with us remaining responsible for their compliance), since our group and outsourced processors need to use the Interface in the ordinary course of the licensed business. We have also confirmed that either party may transfer to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets; if you prefer, we can instead add Affiliates on written notice to TrueLink.

ops.newText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement. For purposes of this Agreement, "Affiliate" means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Client, and Client shall remain responsible for its Affiliates' and contractors' compliance with this Agreement.
ops.oldText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.

ops.newText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets or equity.
ops.oldText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

proposal.summary: Extend licence to Client's Affiliates and contractors and allow transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction

quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
rationale: The grant runs to "Client" only: neither Affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf are licensed, and the only expansion mechanic (amending Exhibit "A" sites on written notice under 2(b)(ii)) covers locations, not additional entities — so there is no path to add Affiliates, which fails the fallback ("Affiliates covered on written notice"). Transfer is also blocked: § 15 requires the other party's consent except for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate, so a successor in an M&A transaction is not covered, again short of the fallback. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (with Client responsible for their compliance) and adds a mutual successor-transfer carve-out. Positively, the licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion (term runs until termination under § 2(c)/§ 13-14), so this is not walk-away territory; we note but do not flag that § 13's automatic cut-off of Sections 2 and 3 for breach of Sections 8a-8c has no cure period, and that the licence is not perpetual/paid-up.

quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, field-of-use or territory restriction on Client. Section 2(a) expressly confirms the opposite of a restriction: Client is free to acquire, develop, license or use competing software and services (subject only to non-infringement of TrueLink IP and the Section 10 confidentiality obligations, per p0024), which meets and exceeds the preferred position. The Client covenants in Section 8 are limited to legal compliance, non-misrepresentation of underwriting decisions, access control, content warranties and anti-spam — none restricts the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The only "compete" reference (p0054, incorporating a separate Non-Competition Agreement) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, i.e. it binds the counterparty and benefits us, so it is not flagged; we note only that that separate agreement is not attached and should be diligenced to confirm it contains no reciprocal restriction on Client.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 gives Client (our party) a unilateral termination-for-convenience right: on written notice, TrueLink continues services only until the last day of the following month, i.e. an effective notice period of roughly 30–60 days, with no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the agreement (the "Section 4" cross-reference is to the minimum monthly fee schedule, and no termination charge exists). TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right — Section 13 lets it exit only by non-renewal of the one-year term, and the initial commitment is 12 months rather than a multi-year term, so the walk-away scenario (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term) does not arise. This meets the preferred position on the material terms. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (moot in practice, since Section 5 bills Hosting and Support Services monthly in arrears within 15 days of invoice, so no fees are prepaid), and TrueLink's end-of-term non-renewal notice is thirty days rather than ninety — a reciprocal right that we hold on identical terms and that benefits us equally.

quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
rationale: The agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection or verification right over Client's usage, records or systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "verify" and "monitor" return nothing, and the two candidate sections confirm this: Compensation (§ 5/6) runs the wrong way for the vendor — Client is entitled to supporting documentation and to contest charges (p0047) — and the Client covenants in § 8 impose compliance and access-restriction duties without any TrueLink right to examine Client's premises, records or systems. Section 2(e) likewise gives Client, not TrueLink, access to usage statistics and raw log files (p0037). The only vendor self-help right is § 8(f), under which TrueLink may "implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming or illegal activity (p0058); that operates within TrueLink's own hosted Interface environment and is neither a usage/records audit nor access to Client systems, so it does not engage the walk-away trigger. With no audit obligation binding us, the rule's protective parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, no system access) cannot be exceeded, so the position is better than preferred. We should not insert an audit right the vendor has not asked for, as that would create an obligation against our own party; we simply resist any audit language added in later drafts unless it meets the once-per-12-months / 30 days' notice / independent auditor / vendor-cost standard.

quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
rationale: Sections 26 and 27 select California law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in California (San Luis Obispo County), with no arbitration and no foreign seat. This sits at the playbook fallback (Delaware or California law and courts) rather than the preferred New York position, so it is acceptable and not redlined. Noted only: venue is fixed in the licensor's local county rather than a neutral California forum, and Section 28 imports California Civil Code section 1717 fee-shifting — both minor sub-elements consistent with a California-law bargain and not independent deviations under this rule.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation running against Client. The sole best-terms provision (Section 6, Documentation and Disputes) is granted by TrueLink in Client's favour: TrueLink's Hosting Services rates may not exceed those charged to any other party, plus a one-year price freeze. I also reviewed Compensation (§5) and Client's covenants and warranties (§8), and searched for "most favored", "no less favorable", "best" and "any other party" language; nothing obliges Client to extend TrueLink terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer, vendor-granted MFN welcome), so no redline is proposed.

quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: The only minimum commitment imposed on Client is the monthly fee floor in § 5(a) (p0045) for Hosting and Support Services. That commitment sits at our fallback position rather than the preferred usage-only position, and is therefore acceptable without redline: (i) it is bounded by a one-year term that auto-renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party able to stop renewal on 30 days' notice (p0078); (ii) Client has a standalone at-will exit under § 14, where services — and hence the monthly minimums — run only to the last day of the month following Client's termination notice (p0079), i.e. roughly a 30-day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, acceleration, or take-or-pay mechanic anywhere in the document, and § 2(a) expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License" (p0022). No multi-year take-or-pay or volume cap on Client usage exists, so walk-away territory is not engaged. Two minor points noted but not flagged as deviations: the § 14 exit is stated as "Subject to Section 4," and § 4 is TrueLink's own commitment to supply a programmer "for a period of not less than ____ months," which could be argued to hold the Support Services minimum open past termination — the blank is unfilled and § 4 reads as a vendor-side obligation benefiting us, so we would clarify only if that blank is completed with a long period. Separately, § 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and dispute rights, which is a billing-transparency point for the audit/disputes rule rather than a minimum-commitment failure. The requirement in § 3(i) (p0042) that Client order a credit report per underwriting approval is a requirements/exclusivity term addressed under that rule, not double-flagged here.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binding the Client. Targeted searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit" and "personnel" returned no restrictive hiring covenant: the "solicit" hits are confined to § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), and the "employ"/"employees" hits are only the § 8(c) access-limitation covenant and the § 12 indemnity beneficiary lists. Full reads of the two likely host sections — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirm Client's only covenants are compliance with laws, non-representation as to underwriting decisions, limiting Interface access, the Credit Data license, content warranties, and confidentiality. This matches our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline is warranted; there is no duration, scope, or general-advertising carve-out to negotiate. Two notes for the file, neither a deviation: (1) § 8(d) references a separate "Non-Competition Agreement" governing use of Credit Data — that instrument is outside this document and should be reviewed separately for any personnel restrictions on Client; and (2) because the rule's preferred outcome is the absence of a clause, this is classified compliant rather than "missing".

quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
rationale: Section 13 (p0078) provides an initial one-year term with automatic renewal for successive one-year (not multi-year) periods, and either party — including us as Client — may prevent renewal by written notice given only 30 days before the end of the then-current year. That 30-day, mutually exercisable non-renewal window and the 12-month renewal term meet the preferred position (well inside the ≤60-day fallback and far from the >90-day walk-away). Two preferred sub-elements are absent and are noted rather than flagged: there is no obligation on TrueLink to send a 60-day renewal reminder, and there is no express CPI/3% cap on renewal pricing — though Section 6 (p0047) freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds an MFN rate commitment, and fees otherwise run off the agreed Exhibit A/B schedule, so TrueLink has no clear unilateral uplift right. We would take the reminder and uplift cap opportunistically if the term is reopened, but neither is a material failure of the rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a transition-assistance and data-return provision to Section 14, since the Agreement currently gives us no right to our own data or to migration help on exit. Our position is up to six months of assistance at your then-current rates with data returned in machine-readable form within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance if that works better for you.

ops.text: Transition Assistance and Return of Client Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems (including backup media, subject to any applicable legal retention requirements) and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, data return within 30 days, and certified deletion into Section 14 (Termination).

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: This is a hosting and licensing agreement in which TrueLink holds Client Content and Credit Data, but no exit provision exists. Section 13 only confirms that Client retains ownership of its domains and Client Content and makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server/hosting environment within 30/60 days; Section 14 merely continues services until the end of the month following notice. Neither obliges TrueLink to provide transition assistance, to return or export our data in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards, and Section 10 contains no return-of-materials mechanic. That falls short of even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition/data-return paragraph in the termination section, noting the 90-day fallback in the comment.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us only a Year 2000 warranty, and Section 11's standard of care is measured against TrueLink's own practices with no remedy, so we have added our standard performance warranty: professional and workmanlike services, 12-month conformance of the Interface and related software to its documentation, no malicious code, and compliance with applicable law, backed by repair, replacement, re-performance or refund. If TrueLink prefers, we can work with a ninety (90) day conformance period.

ops.text: TrueLink further represents and warrants that (a) the Hosting Services, Support Services and any other agreed-upon services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with applicable industry standards; (b) for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications; (c) the Interface and all related software will be free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and other malicious code; and (d) TrueLink will comply in all material respects with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement. Client's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming services, Interface or software, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services, Interface or software.

proposal.summary: Add TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund remedy to Section 9

quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
rationale: TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Year 2000 date-processing warranty; there is no warranty that the Interface or related software conforms to its documentation, no malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's standard of care requires only the care TrueLink "customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard, not industry standard, and it carries no warranty remedy. The disclaimer at p0076 is qualified by "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow express warranties and needs no carve-out; the problem is that there is no express performance warranty to preserve. This fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so we insert the playbook performance warranty at the preferred position (12-month conformance, professional and workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws, repair/replace/refund at TrueLink's option), flagging a 90-day period as an acceptable fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though TrueLink hosts the Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data, so we have added our standard requirement (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). If helpful, we can accept reduced limits of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering TrueLink's hosting of the Web Site and processing of Client Content and other data; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. TrueLink shall provide Client with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry CGL, E&O and cyber liability insurance and provide certificates on request.

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and a review of the miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13-30) and the covenants and indemnity sections confirms the Agreement imposes no insurance obligation on TrueLink. TrueLink hosts the Client's Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data through the Interface, so the rule's walk-away scenario (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data) applies; the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is likewise unmet. We therefore insert a new Section 31 at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), placed after Section 30 as the last substantive miscellaneous clause, with the fallback limits offered in the comment.
